text: To-day: Helen is back at Stoke Moran, waiting eagerly for Holmes and Watson
why: Helen has come back to Stoke Moran and says she has been waiting eagerly for them (¶126).

text: That afternoon: Holmes and Watson come to Stoke Moran as promised, and Miss Stoner hurries to meet them
why: Holmes said they would come early in the afternoon (¶82), and they arrive at the house where Helen hurries forward to greet them (¶123, ¶126).

text: This evening at the earliest: Dr. Roylott is expected back
why: Helen says Roylott is unlikely to be back before evening (¶126), so evening at the earliest follows directly.

text: When will Dr. Roylott come back to Stoke Moran?
why: A plain question; Helen's statement that he is unlikely back before evening gives the reader reason to ask it.

text: When will Dr. Roylott come back to Stoke Moran? — not before evening
why: Helen states that it is unlikely he will be back before evening (¶126).

text: When will Dr. Roylott come back to Stoke Moran? — sooner than she expects, while the rooms are being examined
id: q.roylott_back=sooner than she expects, while the rooms are being examined
why: The story has established Roylott as violent and suspicious of Holmes's inquiry (¶104–111), Holmes plans to see the rooms (¶76), and Helen's 'unlikely' hedge leaves a sooner return open, so a reader has reason to consider it.
